title: calculateRiskLevel() maps score to level using the canonical 20/15/10/5 thresholds
description: risk-management-service/src/utils/validation.ts calculateRiskLevel() is the single source of truth for score-to-level mapping used by RiskScoreSchema's transform. Verifies boundary values on both sides of each threshold.
expectedResult: Returns 'critical' for >=20, 'high' for 15-19, 'medium' for 10-14, 'low' for 5-9, 'info' for <5 — with no off-by-one at any boundary.

title: RiskScoreSchema always derives score/level server-side, ignoring any client-supplied score or level
description: RiskScoreSchema.transform() in validation.ts recomputes score = likelihood * impact and level = calculateRiskLevel(score) unconditionally, so a client cannot forge a lower risk level by sending a mismatched score/level alongside likelihood/impact.
steps: Parse RiskScoreSchema with { likelihood: 5, impact: 5, score: 1, level: 'info' }
expectedResult: Parsed output has score=25 and level='critical' — the forged score/level inputs are discarded, not honored.

title: ModuleRiskService.severityToScore() uses different level thresholds than calculateRiskLevel()
description: ModuleRiskService.severityToScore() and BaseIntegrationService.severityToScore() classify a score>=20 as critical, >=12 as high, >=6 as medium, else low (no 'info' tier) — this differs from validation.ts calculateRiskLevel()'s 20/15/10/5 thresholds used for manually-scored risks. A 'high' severity module risk (4x4=16) promotes as level 'high' under this formula but would be 'high' under calculateRiskLevel too (15-19), while a 'medium' severity module risk (3x3=9) promotes as 'medium' here but would be 'low' under calculateRiskLevel (5-9). Documents the discrepancy so auto-promoted and manually-scored risks of the same score aren't silently misclassified against each other.
steps: Compare against calculateRiskLevel(9) from validation.ts → expect 'low'
expectedResult: Confirms the two scoring formulas disagree at score=9 (medium via module-risk promotion vs low via manual assessment). Flagged for product decision on whether promotion severity should use the same thresholds as manual assessment.

title: isValidPhaseTransition() rejects skipping identification straight to mitigation
description: RiskRegisterService.isValidPhaseTransition() (private) defines the RMF phase graph: identification -> [assessment, closure]; assessment -> [identification, mitigation, monitoring, closure]; mitigation -> [assessment, monitoring, closure]; monitoring -> [mitigation, closure]; closure -> [monitoring]. A risk must pass through assessment before mitigation.
steps: Call movePhase with targetPhase='mitigation' while risk.phase='identification'
expectedResult: Request fails with 400 'Invalid phase transition from identification to mitigation'.

title: closure phase can only re-enter monitoring, never directly back to mitigation
steps: Call movePhase with targetPhase='mitigation' while risk.phase='closure'
Call movePhase with targetPhase='monitoring' while risk.phase='closure'
expectedResult: The first call is rejected (400, invalid transition); the second succeeds — closure can only reopen into monitoring, matching the documented 'Can reopen from closure' transition table.

title: AcceptanceRequestSchema rejects a justification shorter than 50 characters
description: AcceptanceRequestSchema.justification enforces min(50) with the explicit message 'Justification must be at least 50 characters to constitute adequate documented rationale' — same rule applies to RenewalRequestSchema.
steps: Parse AcceptanceRequestSchema with justification='Too short', validUntil=<future date>, approverIds=[<valid ObjectId>]
expectedResult: Zod validation fails with a message referencing the 50-character minimum; POST /risks/:riskId/acceptance/request returns 400 with field-level details.

title: AcceptanceRequestSchema requires at least one and at most ten approverIds
steps: Parse AcceptanceRequestSchema with 11 distinct valid ObjectId strings in approverIds
expectedResult: Both parses fail validation — empty approverIds violates min(1), 11 entries violates max(10).

title: EscalateRiskRequestSchema clamps escalation level to 1-3 and defaults to 1
description: EscalateRiskRequestSchema requires reason min(10) chars and level is an int between 1 and 3, defaulting to 1 when omitted — matching the L1/L2/L3 escalation tiers shown in GovernanceMetrics.escalatedRisks.
steps: Parse EscalateRiskRequestSchema omitting 'level' with a valid reason of 10+ characters
expectedResult: First parse succeeds with level defaulted to 1; second parse fails because 4 is outside the 1-3 range.

title: generateRiskCode() returns null when no projectId is supplied instead of falling back to a misleading project
description: A prior implementation fell back to 'the org's earliest-created project' when projectId was absent, silently producing a riskCode that implied the wrong origin. The current generateRiskCode() in utils/riskCode.ts returns null in that case and never throws.
expectedResult: Function resolves to null (not a throw, not a code derived from an unrelated project).

title: notificationWindowMs() returns a shorter dedup window than the review interval so a missed run is never permanently silenced
description: review-scheduler.job.ts intentionally sizes the dedup window shorter than each reviewFrequency interval (Monthly=25d vs a ~30d cycle, Quarterly=80d, Semi-Annual=170d, Annual=350d) so a skipped daily job run doesn't leave the notification suppressed forever.
steps: Call notificationWindowMs('Monthly'), ('Quarterly'), ('Semi-Annual'), ('Annual'), and an unrecognized string
expectedResult: Returns 25/80/170/350 days in ms respectively, and falls back to the Annual (350-day) window for any unrecognized frequency string.
